**Finding: deviation (rule T4C — Termination for convenience)**

- **Vendor side (compliant):** Array has no convenience right. Its termination routes are material breach (13.3), bankruptcy (13.4) and Ono's Competing Product breach (8.2). No redline needed.
- **Customer side (fails fallback):** Section 13.1 runs to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term, but our at-will right in 13.2 only switches on after the later of a redacted period following First Commercial Sale of *both* Products — so throughout development and pre-launch we have no convenience exit (only the narrow Safety/Efficacy rights in 13.5). That is the walk-away scenario ("no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term").

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** amend 13.2 so Ono may terminate at any time, in whole or Product-by-Product, on ninety (90) days' written notice — fallback notice length, which is proportionate given the Article XIV wind-down mechanics.

Noted in the rationale but not separately flagged: the redacted notice period in 13.2 should be confirmed at 30–90 days; and the Ono-borne wind-down/transfer costs (14.2(a)) plus the post-termination Competing Product restriction (8.2) are economic consequences of an at-will exit better handled under the pricing/exclusivity rules than double-flagged here.
